description: Question bank derived from 'Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records' - comprehensive coverage of all sections including world records, India records, Karnataka records, locations, terminology, and exam traps.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the highest point on Earth above mean sea level?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest, in the Himalaya on the Nepal-China (Tibet) border, is the highest mountain summit above mean sea level at 8,848.86 m under the jointly announced 2020 Nepal-China elevation.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the deepest known point in the oceans?
questions.explanation: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, western Pacific Ocean, is the deepest known ocean point. Exact depth estimates vary with survey method and reference datum; commonly reported measurements are around 10.9-11.0 km below sea level.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the lowest exposed land point on Earth?
questions.explanation: The shore of the Dead Sea, between Israel and Jordan and adjoining the West Bank, is the lowest exposed land elevation. Its level changes over time because of water loss and inflow changes; it is roughly 430 m below mean sea level in recent years.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest continent by area and population?
questions.explanation: Asia is the largest continent by area and population.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is conventionally the smallest continent by area?
questions.explanation: Australia is conventionally the smallest continent by area; some geographical classifications use Oceania for the wider region of Australia, New Zealand and Pacific islands.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest and deepest ocean basin?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean basin.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the smallest and shallowest of the five commonly recognised oceans?
questions.explanation: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest of the five commonly recognised oceans.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river is traditionally listed as the longest river in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile is traditionally listed as the longest river, at about 6,650 km. Some studies argue for the Amazon depending on source selection and measurement method. For conventional competitive-exam answers, Nile is the standard response.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river has the greatest average discharge and largest drainage basin?
questions.explanation: The Amazon has the greatest average discharge and the largest drainage basin of any river system. It drains a vast part of northern South America into the Atlantic Ocean.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the longest river in Asia?
questions.explanation: The Yangtze (Chang Jiang) in China, about 6,300 km, is generally recognised as Asia's longest river.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the second-highest mountain summit above sea level?
questions.explanation: K2 (8,611 m) is the second-highest summit, located in the Karakoram on the Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan/China border region.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the height of Kangchenjunga, the third-highest mountain peak?
questions.explanation: Kangchenjunga stands at 8,586 m and is commonly listed among the world's highest peaks after Everest and K2.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the height of Lhotse, one of the world's highest peaks?
questions.explanation: Lhotse stands at 8,516 m and is commonly listed among the world's highest peaks after Everest.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the height of Makalu, one of the world's highest peaks?
questions.explanation: Makalu stands at 8,485 m and is commonly listed among the world's highest peaks after Everest.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara in North Africa is the largest hot desert. Antarctica is the largest desert overall because deserts are defined by low precipitation, not by high temperature.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest desert overall in the world?
questions.explanation: Antarctica is the largest desert overall because deserts are defined by low precipitation, not by high temperature.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest island in the world under the usual convention that Australia is a continent?
questions.explanation: Greenland is the world's largest island under the usual convention that Australia is a continent rather than an island.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest enclosed inland body of water by surface area?
questions.explanation: The Caspian Sea is the largest enclosed inland body of water by surface area, despite being called a sea.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest freshwater lake by surface area?
questions.explanation: If the question asks for the largest freshwater lake by surface area, the answer is Lake Superior.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake and contains the largest volume of unfrozen freshwater in a lake.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the world's largest delta?
questions.explanation: The Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta, also called the Bengal Delta or Sundarbans delta region, is generally identified as the world's largest delta. It spans Bangladesh and India.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which country is generally ranked as having the world's longest coastline?
questions.explanation: Canada is generally ranked as having the world's longest coastline, although coastline length depends strongly on measurement scale and mapping method—the coastline paradox.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the deepest lake in Africa?
questions.explanation: Lake Tanganyika is Africa's deepest lake and one of the world's deepest freshwater lakes.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which lake is commonly cited as the world's highest large navigable lake?
questions.explanation: Lake Titicaca, on the Peru-Bolivia border in the Andes, is commonly cited as the world's highest large navigable lake, at about 3,812 m above sea level. 'Navigable' depends on vessel and definition.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the world's largest coral reef system?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef off Queensland, Australia, is the world's largest coral reef system.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is generally identified as the world's largest peninsula?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Peninsula is generally identified as the world's largest peninsula.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major geographical extreme of the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake, not Lake Victoria. Examples of major geographical extremes include the Sahara (largest hot desert), Antarctica (largest desert), Greenland (largest island), Pacific (largest ocean), Mariana Trench (deepest ocean trench), Everest (highest summit), Dead Sea shore (lowest exposed land), and Amazon (greatest river discharge).
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which peak is the highest peak entirely within Indian-administered territory?
questions.explanation: The highest peak entirely within Indian-administered territory is often given as Nanda Devi (7,816 m), subject to the precise territorial definition used. K2 is in territory claimed by India but administered by Pakistan; Kangchenjunga is shared with Nepal.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the southernmost point of India's territory?
questions.explanation: Indira Point on Great Nicobar Island is the southernmost point of India's territory. Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the southernmost point of mainland India?
questions.explanation: Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest Indian state by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan is the largest Indian state by area.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the smallest Indian state by area?
questions.explanation: Goa is the smallest state by area.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Among Union Territories, which is the largest by area?
questions.explanation: Among Union Territories, Ladakh is the largest by area and Lakshadweep the smallest.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.question: Among Union Territories, which is the smallest by area?

options.D: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river is commonly identified as India's longest river by length within the country in standard exam material?
questions.explanation: The Ganga is commonly identified as India's longest river by length within the country in standard exam material. Exact ranking can depend on whether the river's transboundary total course or only the Indian stretch is measured.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river is the longest river of peninsular India and is often called the Dakshin Ganga?
questions.explanation: The Godavari is the longest river of peninsular India and is often called the Dakshin Ganga.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which lake in Jammu and Kashmir is commonly described as one of India's largest freshwater lakes?
questions.explanation: Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir is commonly described as one of India's largest freshwater lakes; its area fluctuates seasonally.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is India's largest brackish-water lagoon and a Ramsar site?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake in Odisha is India's largest brackish-water lagoon and is a Ramsar site.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is India's largest inland salt lake?
questions.explanation: Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan is India's largest inland salt lake.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which waterfall is commonly listed as India's highest waterfall by total height?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls in Karnataka is commonly listed as India's highest waterfall by total height (about 455 m). Waterfall rankings can vary by definition, number of drops, seasonal flow and survey method.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Among Indian states, which has the longest coastline under the revised official measurement?
questions.explanation: Among Indian states, Gujarat has the longest coastline under the revised official measurement. India's national coastline figure was revised to 11,098.81 km in 2025; older textbooks quote 7,516.6 km.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Indian state has the largest forest cover by area according to the India State of Forest Report 2023?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover by area in the India State of Forest Report 2023. Forest cover percentage and total forest area are different measures; Mizoram and other northeastern states rank highly by percentage.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the highest peak in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Mullayanagiri in Chikkamagaluru district, approximately 1,930 m above sea level, is Karnataka's highest peak.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which waterfall is commonly cited as Karnataka's highest waterfall and India's highest by total height?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls on the Varahi River in Shivamogga district is commonly cited as Karnataka's highest waterfall and India's highest by total height. Its visible flow is highly dependent on rainfall and reservoir regulation.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the four named cascades of Jog Falls?
questions.explanation: Jog Falls on the Sharavathi River has four named cascades: Raja, Rani, Rover and Rocket.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is commonly listed as Karnataka's largest district by area under the current 31-district administrative arrangement?
questions.explanation: Belagavi is commonly listed as Karnataka's largest district by area under the current 31-district administrative arrangement; check current state statistical tables if an exam asks for a precise ranking.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is generally listed as the smallest district by area among Karnataka's districts?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru Urban is generally listed as the smallest district by area among Karnataka's districts.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a main river basin of Karnataka?

options.D: West-flowing river basins such as Sharavathi

questions.explanation: The main river basins of Karnataka include the Krishna basin in the north and east; the Cauvery basin in the south and southeast; west-flowing river basins such as Sharavathi, Kali, Netravati, Aghanashini and Varahi; and smaller basins/tributaries associated with the Godavari and Pennar systems. The Ganga basin is not a main river basin of Karnataka.
questions.source: Important Geographical Facts, Locations and Records - 3.12.1

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a geographical superlative?

options.A: A geographical feature located only in tropical regions
options.B: A record describing an extreme geographical feature
options.C: A geographical boundary between two countries

questions.explanation: A geographical superlative describes an extreme feature such as the highest, lowest, largest, smallest, longest, deepest or most extensive. The measurement and geographical scope must be specified.

questions.explanation: Karnataka is not crossed by the Tropic of Cancer. It lies south of this important latitude.
