questions.question: Zoji La is an important mountain pass connecting which two regions?
questions.explanation: Zoji La is an important Himalayan mountain pass on the route connecting Kashmir with Ladakh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Nathu La is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Nathu La is an important mountain pass in Sikkim connecting India with the Tibet region of China.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mountain pass is associated with the Uttarakhand-Tibet border region?
questions.explanation: Mana Pass is an important Himalayan pass associated with the Uttarakhand-Tibet border region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mountain pass is located in Himachal Pradesh and associated with the India-Tibet route?
questions.explanation: Shipki La is an important mountain pass in Himachal Pradesh associated with the route towards Tibet.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pass is associated with the route through Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Bomdi La and Se La are important mountain passes in Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geographical gap lies between the Nilgiri and Anaimalai ranges?
questions.explanation: The Palakkad Gap lies between the Nilgiri and Anaimalai ranges in the Kerala-Tamil Nadu region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important mountain route in Karnataka's Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: Agumbe Ghat is an important route through the Western Ghats in Karnataka. Charmadi and Shiradi are other important Karnataka ghat routes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the geographical term for the point where two or more rivers or streams join?
questions.explanation: A confluence is the point at which two or more rivers or streams meet and join.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At which place do the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers meet to form the Ganga?
questions.explanation: The Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers meet at Devprayag in Uttarakhand. From this confluence, the river is known as the Ganga.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two rivers meet at Rudraprayag?
questions.explanation: Rudraprayag is the confluence of the Alaknanda and Mandakini rivers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two rivers meet at Karnaprayag?
questions.explanation: Karnaprayag is the confluence of the Alaknanda and Pindar rivers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At which place do the Ganga and Yamuna rivers meet?
questions.explanation: The Ganga and Yamuna meet at Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. The traditional third river, Saraswati, is regarded as sacred or subterranean in religious tradition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which port was formerly known as Kandla Port?
questions.explanation: Kandla Port in Gujarat was renamed Deendayal Port. It is situated on the Gulf of Kutch.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Jawaharlal Nehru Port is also popularly known by which name?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru Port, located near Mumbai in Maharashtra, is popularly known as Nhava Sheva.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: New Mangalore Port is located in which state?
questions.explanation: New Mangalore Port is situated at Panambur near Mangaluru in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which port is associated with the former name Tuticorin?
questions.explanation: V.O. Chidambaranar Port, formerly Tuticorin Port, is located in Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Kamarajar Port is also known by which former name?
questions.explanation: Kamarajar Port, situated near Chennai in Tamil Nadu, was formerly known as Ennore Port.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are located in which water body?
questions.explanation: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are located in the Bay of Bengal and include islands with volcanic and coral features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Lakshadweep is located in which sea?
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep is an island group in the Arabian Sea, consisting mainly of coral atolls.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following islands belongs to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands group?
questions.explanation: Great Nicobar is part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands group in the Bay of Bengal. Minicoy, Kavaratti and Agatti belong to Lakshadweep.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following islands belongs to Lakshadweep?
questions.explanation: Minicoy is an important island of Lakshadweep in the Arabian Sea. Little Andaman, North Sentinel and Great Nicobar belong to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important iron ore-producing mineral belt in eastern India?
questions.explanation: The Odisha–Jharkhand belt is one of India's important iron ore mineral belts. Other important belts include Durg–Bastar–Chandrapur, Ballari–Chitradurga–Chikkamagaluru–Tumakuru and Maharashtra–Goa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important iron ore belt in central India?
questions.explanation: The Durg–Bastar–Chandrapur belt is an important iron ore-producing region extending across parts of Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important iron ore belt in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Ballari–Chitradurga–Chikkamagaluru–Tumakuru belt is an important iron ore-producing region of Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Maharashtra–Goa mineral belt is particularly associated with the production of which mineral?
questions.explanation: The Maharashtra–Goa belt is one of India's important iron ore-producing regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which valley is an important coal-producing region of India?
questions.explanation: The Damodar Valley is an important coal-producing region of eastern India, particularly in Jharkhand and West Bengal.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as an important coal-bearing region of India?
questions.explanation: The Son–Mahanadi region is an important coal-bearing belt of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river valley is associated with coal deposits in southern India?
questions.explanation: The Godavari Valley is an important coal-bearing region of India, particularly in the Telangana region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following states is an important producer of bauxite in India?
questions.explanation: Odisha is one of India's important bauxite-producing states. Other important states include Gujarat, Jharkhand, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group contains only states identified in the PDF as important bauxite-producing regions?
questions.explanation: Odisha, Gujarat and Jharkhand are among the important bauxite-producing states listed in the PDF. Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh are also included.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following states is an important manganese-producing state according to the PDF?
questions.explanation: Karnataka is listed among the important manganese-producing states of India, along with Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group correctly represents important manganese-producing states listed in the PDF?

options.A: Odisha, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Odisha, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra as important manganese-producing states.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important petroleum and natural gas-producing region of India?
questions.explanation: Mumbai offshore is an important petroleum and natural gas-producing region of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which sedimentary basin is associated with petroleum and natural gas resources in eastern coastal India?
questions.explanation: The Krishna–Godavari Basin is an important petroleum and natural gas-bearing region of eastern coastal India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group correctly identifies important petroleum and natural gas regions of India?

options.A: Assam–Arakan, Gujarat, Mumbai offshore and Krishna–Godavari Basin
options.B: Damodar, Son–Mahanadi, Godavari and Chota Nagpur
options.C: Odisha, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh

questions.explanation: The PDF identifies Assam–Arakan, Gujarat, Mumbai offshore and the Krishna–Godavari Basin as important petroleum and natural gas regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which crop dominates much of eastern, northeastern and coastal India?
questions.explanation: Rice is the dominant crop across much of eastern, northeastern, coastal and irrigated southern India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which crop is concentrated mainly in the northwestern and northern plains of India?
questions.explanation: Wheat is concentrated in the northwestern and northern plains of India, particularly in major agricultural states of the Indo-Gangetic region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Cotton cultivation in India is particularly associated with which soil region?
questions.explanation: Cotton cultivation is strongly associated with the Deccan and black-soil regions of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group of states is specifically identified as an important sugarcane-growing region in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka are identified as important sugarcane-producing states in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Indian state is particularly famous for tea cultivation?
questions.explanation: Assam is one of India's major tea-producing regions. The PDF also identifies West Bengal and southern hill regions as important tea-growing areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group correctly represents important tea-growing regions mentioned in the PDF?

options.A: Assam, West Bengal and southern hill regions

questions.explanation: Tea is concentrated in Assam, West Bengal and the southern hill regions of India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Indian state is especially important for coffee cultivation?
questions.explanation: Karnataka is a leading coffee-growing state in India. Kerala and Tamil Nadu are also identified as important coffee-growing states in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which crops are commonly associated with the semi-arid Deccan region and Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Millets and pulses are important crops in the semi-arid Deccan region and Rajasthan.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following crop-region pairs is incorrectly matched according to the geographical distribution described in the PDF?

options.C: Coffee — Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu

questions.explanation: Tea is concentrated in Assam, West Bengal and southern hill regions, not the Rajasthan desert region. The other pairs correctly represent important crop distributions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important industrial region of western India?
questions.explanation: Mumbai–Pune is one of India's important industrial regions, with a wide range of manufacturing and service industries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Ahmedabad–Vadodara is an important industrial region of which state?
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad–Vadodara is an important industrial region in Gujarat.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which group represents important industrial centres in the Chota Nagpur mineral-industrial region?
questions.explanation: Jamshedpur, Bokaro and Rourkela are important industrial centres associated with the eastern Indian mineral-industrial belt.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important industrial centre in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru is a major industrial and technological centre in Karnataka and is included among India's important industrial centres.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only industrial centres listed in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Visakhapatnam, Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad are all identified as important industrial centres in India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Jim Corbett National Park is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Jim Corbett National Park is located in Uttarakhand and is India's oldest national park, established in 1936 as Hailey National Park.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Kaziranga National Park is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga National Park is located in Assam and is internationally famous for its population of the greater one-horned rhinoceros.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two important national parks are located in Assam?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga and Manas are two important national parks in Assam, both recognised for their ecological importance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Gir National Park is situated in which state?
questions.explanation: Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary in Gujarat is famous for the Asiatic lion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Ranthambore National Park is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Ranthambore National Park is located in Rajasthan and is widely known for its tiger population.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pair of national parks is located in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Kanha and Bandhavgarh National Parks are located in Madhya Pradesh and are important tiger habitats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Sundarbans National Park is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Sundarbans National Park is located in West Bengal and forms part of the extensive mangrove ecosystem of the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Periyar National Park is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Periyar National Park is situated in Kerala and is an important protected area associated with the Western Ghats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only national parks located in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Bandipur, Nagarahole and Kudremukh are important national parks in Karnataka, recognised for their biodiversity and forest ecosystems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Keibul Lamjao National Park is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Keibul Lamjao National Park is located in Manipur on Loktak Lake and is famous for its floating phumdi habitat and the endangered sangai deer.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important biosphere reserve in southern India?
questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is an important biosphere reserve in southern India, spanning parts of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which biosphere reserve is associated with the Gulf of Mannar?
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve is located along the southeastern coast of India in Tamil Nadu and is known for its marine biodiversity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the general administrative distinction between major and non-major ports in India?

options.A: Major ports are classified solely by cargo volume.
options.B: Major ports fall under the Union government's major-port framework, while non-major ports are generally administered by state maritime boards or state governments.
options.C: All non-major ports are privately owned.
options.D: Major ports are administered exclusively by district administrations.

questions.explanation: The classification is based on the applicable legal and administrative framework. Major ports fall under the Union government's major-port framework, while other ports are generally administered by state maritime boards or state governments. The distinction is not simply based on cargo volume.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the highest peak in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Mullayanagiri in Chikkamagaluru district is the highest peak in Karnataka, with an approximate elevation of 1,930 metres.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which district is Mullayanagiri located?
questions.explanation: Mullayanagiri is situated in Chikkamagaluru district in the Western Ghats of Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the approximate elevation of Mullayanagiri?
questions.explanation: Mullayanagiri has an approximate elevation of 1,930 metres above sea level and is Karnataka's highest peak.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is commonly cited as the highest waterfall in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls on the Varahi River in Shivamogga district is commonly cited as Karnataka's highest waterfall, with an approximate total height of 455 metres.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is commonly listed as India's highest waterfall by total height?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls in Karnataka is commonly listed as India's highest waterfall by total height, approximately 455 metres. Rankings depend on the definition, number of drops, seasonal flow and survey method.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which district is commonly listed as the largest district in Karnataka by area under the 31-district administrative arrangement?
questions.explanation: Belagavi is commonly listed as Karnataka's largest district by area under the current 31-district administrative arrangement. Exact rankings should be checked against current state statistical tables.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which district is generally listed as the smallest district in Karnataka by geographical area?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru Urban is generally listed as the smallest district in Karnataka by area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river basin occupies much of northern and eastern Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Krishna basin occupies a large part of northern and eastern Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river basin is mainly associated with southern and southeastern Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Cauvery basin covers much of southern and southeastern Karnataka and extends into Tamil Nadu and other adjoining regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only west-flowing rivers of Karnataka?

options.A: Sharavathi, Kali, Netravati, Aghanashini and Varahi

questions.explanation: Sharavathi, Kali, Netravati, Aghanashini and Varahi are important west-flowing rivers of Karnataka. They drain towards the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two additional river systems are mentioned in connection with smaller basins and tributaries of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Apart from the major Krishna and Cauvery basins and west-flowing river basins, smaller basins and tributaries associated with the Godavari and Pennar systems are also found in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Talakaveri is situated in which district of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Talakaveri is located in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu district and is traditionally regarded as the source of the Cauvery River.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Talakaveri is traditionally regarded as the source of which river?
questions.explanation: Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu district is traditionally regarded as the source of the Cauvery River.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about the source of the Cauvery at Talakaveri is geographically accurate?

options.A: The river originates exclusively from a single visible lake.
options.B: A temple and sacred tank mark the traditional source area, while actual headwater hydrology includes surrounding springs and streams.
options.C: The Cauvery originates from a glacier in the Himalayas.
options.D: Talakaveri is located in the coastal plains of Karnataka.

questions.explanation: Talakaveri has a temple and sacred tank marking the traditional source area. The river's actual headwater hydrology involves springs and streams in the surrounding highlands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Kudremukh is located in which district of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kudremukh is a mountain and protected landscape in the Western Ghats of Chikkamagaluru district.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Kudremukh is particularly associated with which protected area?
questions.explanation: Kudremukh is associated with Kudremukh National Park, an important protected landscape in the Western Ghats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which ecological features are associated with the Kudremukh landscape?
questions.explanation: The Kudremukh landscape is associated with montane grasslands, shola forests and rich Western Ghats biodiversity. It also has a history of iron-ore mining.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Jog Falls is located on which river?
questions.explanation: Jog Falls is formed by the Sharavathi River in Shivamogga district of Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which district is Jog Falls located?
questions.explanation: Jog Falls is situated in Shivamogga district on the Sharavathi River.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the four major cascades of Jog Falls?
questions.explanation: The four major cascades of Jog Falls are Raja, Rani, Rover and Rocket.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which factors strongly influence the flow of Jog Falls?

options.C: Tidal movements of the Arabian Sea

questions.explanation: The flow of Jog Falls is strongly seasonal and is influenced by southwest monsoon rainfall and upstream reservoir operations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Kunchikal Falls is formed by which river?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls is situated on the Varahi River in Shivamogga district.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Near which region is Kunchikal Falls located?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls is located on the Varahi River near the Hulikal region in Shivamogga district.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the approximate total height commonly quoted for Kunchikal Falls?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls is commonly quoted as approximately 455 metres in total height. Its visible flow depends on rainfall and reservoir regulation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Shivanasamudra Falls is located on which river?
questions.explanation: Shivanasamudra Falls is formed by the Cauvery River in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two major waterfalls are formed at Shivanasamudra?
questions.explanation: At Shivanasamudra, the Cauvery divides around an island and forms the Gaganachukki and Bharachukki waterfalls.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Shivanasamudra Falls is located in which district according to the PDF?
questions.explanation: Shivanasamudra Falls is located in Mandya district on the Cauvery River.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Shivanasamudra Falls is historically associated with which development?
questions.explanation: Shivanasamudra Falls is associated with an early hydroelectric power station, an important development in the history of electricity generation in India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Gokak Falls is formed by which river?
questions.explanation: Gokak Falls is situated on the Ghataprabha River near Gokak in Belagavi district.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which district is Gokak Falls located?
questions.explanation: Gokak Falls is located near Gokak in Belagavi district, Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the distinctive physical feature of the gorge at Gokak Falls?
questions.explanation: The Ghataprabha River drops over a horseshoe-shaped rocky gorge at Gokak Falls. A nearby suspension bridge is a well-known landmark.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Hampi is situated in the valley of which river?
questions.explanation: Hampi is situated in the Tungabhadra River valley in Vijayanagara district of Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Hampi is located in which district of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Hampi is located in Vijayanagara district, Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geological feature gives the Hampi landscape its distinctive appearance?
questions.explanation: Hampi is characterised by a distinctive granite boulder landscape, a riverine setting and dry deciduous vegetation. Its historic Vijayanagara monuments form part of a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Nandi Hills is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Nandi Hills is a hill complex in Chikkaballapur district, northeast of Bengaluru.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes Nandi Hills from Mullayanagiri?

options.A: Nandi Hills is Karnataka's highest peak.
options.B: Mullayanagiri is Karnataka's highest peak, while Nandi Hills is a hill complex near Bengaluru.
options.C: Both are located in Kodagu district.
options.D: Nandi Hills is situated on the Arabian Sea coast.

questions.explanation: Mullayanagiri is Karnataka's highest peak. Nandi Hills is a prominent hill complex in Chikkaballapur district and is not the state's highest peak.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Biligiriranga Hills are mainly located in which district of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Biligiriranga Hills, also called B.R. Hills, lie in southern Karnataka, mainly in Chamarajanagar district.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the ecological significance of the Biligiriranga Hills?

options.A: They form a link between the Western and Eastern Ghats.
options.B: They separate the Himalayas from the Karakoram.
options.C: They form the boundary between the Thar Desert and the Aravallis.
options.D: They connect the Nilgiri Hills with the Himalayas.

questions.explanation: The B.R. Hills form an important ecological link between the Western and Eastern Ghats. The BRT Tiger Reserve protects diverse forest habitats and wildlife.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which protected reserve is associated with the Biligiriranga Hills?
questions.explanation: The Biligiriranga Hills are associated with the Biligiri Rangaswamy Temple (BRT) Tiger Reserve in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Agumbe is popularly known by which geographical nickname?
questions.explanation: Agumbe in Shivamogga district is known as the Cherrapunji of the South because it receives very heavy southwest monsoon rainfall due to orographic uplift along the Western Ghats.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Yana, famous for its distinctive dark rock formations, is located in which district of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Yana is situated in Uttara Kannada district in the Western Ghats region of Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two prominent rock formations are associated with Yana?
questions.explanation: The two well-known rock formations at Yana are Bhairaveshwara Shikhara and Mohini Shikhara.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The distinctive rock formations at Yana are primarily associated with which type of rock?
questions.explanation: Yana is known for its dark limestone or karst rock formations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Yana rock formations are located in which geographical region?
questions.explanation: Yana is located in the Western Ghats of Uttara Kannada district and is surrounded by forest.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a coastal town and port in Uttara Kannada district?
questions.explanation: Karwar is a coastal town and port in Uttara Kannada district, near the Kali River estuary and the Goa border.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Karwar is situated near the estuary of which river?
questions.explanation: Karwar is located near the Kali River estuary in Uttara Kannada district.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Gokarna, known for its beaches and pilgrimage importance, is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Gokarna is a coastal pilgrimage and beach town in Uttara Kannada district, known for its rocky shoreline and beaches.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Malpe, an important fishing harbour and beach, is situated near which city?
questions.explanation: Malpe is a fishing harbour and beach near Udupi. It is also a departure point for visits to St. Mary's Islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: St. Mary's Islands are located off the coast of which place in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: St. Mary's Islands are situated off Malpe, near Udupi, on the Karnataka coast.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: St. Mary's Islands are particularly famous for which geological feature?
questions.explanation: St. Mary's Islands are known for columnar basalt formations created by ancient volcanic activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How many coastal districts does Karnataka have?
questions.explanation: Karnataka has three coastal districts: Uttara Kannada, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists Karnataka's three coastal districts?

options.A: Uttara Kannada, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada

questions.explanation: The three coastal districts of Karnataka are Uttara Kannada, Udupi and Dakshina Kannada.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Karwar is in Uttara Kannada. Malpe is near Udupi, Panambur is associated with Mangaluru, and Gokarna is in Uttara Kannada.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Netravati–Gurupura estuarine region is associated with which coastal city?
questions.explanation: The Netravati–Gurupura estuarine region is an important part of the coastal geography around Mangaluru.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Almatti Dam is constructed across which river?
questions.explanation: Almatti Dam is built across the Krishna River in Vijayapura district and is associated with the Upper Krishna Project.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Almatti Dam is an important component of which irrigation project?
questions.explanation: Almatti Dam is a major structure associated with the Upper Krishna Project.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Tungabhadra Dam is constructed across which river?
questions.explanation: Tungabhadra Dam is constructed across the Tungabhadra River near Hospet, in present-day Vijayanagara district.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a major purpose of Tungabhadra Dam in the reference material?
questions.explanation: The reference identifies irrigation, hydropower and water supply as important functions of Tungabhadra Dam. Marine navigation is not listed.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) Dam is built across which river?
questions.explanation: KRS Dam is constructed across the Cauvery River near Srirangapatna in the Mandya region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which famous garden is associated with Krishna Raja Sagara Dam?
questions.explanation: Brindavan Gardens is located near KRS Dam and is one of the well-known attractions associated with the reservoir.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Linganamakki Dam is constructed across which river?
questions.explanation: Linganamakki Dam is built across the Sharavathi River in Shivamogga district and is an important reservoir for the Sharavathi hydroelectric system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which major waterfall is located downstream of Linganamakki Dam on the Sharavathi River?
questions.explanation: Linganamakki Dam is situated upstream of Jog Falls on the Sharavathi River.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Supa Dam is associated with which river?
questions.explanation: Supa Dam is built across the Kali River near Joida in Uttara Kannada district and is part of the Kali hydroelectric system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Hutti Gold Mines are located in which district of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Hutti Gold Mines are located in Raichur district and are an important operating gold-mining centre in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Karnataka gold-mining region is historically famous for deep underground mining and large-scale operations that closed in 2001?
questions.explanation: Kolar Gold Fields (KGF), in Kolar district, is historically known for deep gold mining. Large-scale mining operations closed in 2001.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pair correctly matches the Karnataka gold-mining centres with their districts?

options.A: Hutti — Raichur; Kolar Gold Fields — Kolar
options.B: Hutti — Kolar; Kolar Gold Fields — Raichur
options.C: Hutti — Ballari; Kolar Gold Fields — Vijayapura
options.D: Hutti — Udupi; Kolar Gold Fields — Hassan

questions.explanation: Hutti Gold Mines are located in Raichur district, while Kolar Gold Fields are located in Kolar district.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Ballari–Hospet region of Karnataka is particularly important for the mining of which mineral?
questions.explanation: The Ballari–Hospet region is an important iron-ore belt in eastern Karnataka and is associated with steel and related industries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Ballari–Hospet iron-ore belt is significant mainly because of its connection with which industrial sector?
questions.explanation: Iron ore from the Ballari–Hospet region is linked to the development of steel and related industries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which environmental issue is specifically associated with mining activities in the Ballari–Hospet region?
questions.explanation: The reference identifies environmental impacts as an important concern associated with mining in the Ballari–Hospet iron-ore belt.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Pavagada Solar Park is located in which district of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Pavagada Solar Park, also known as Shakti Sthala, is situated in Pavagada taluk of Tumakuru district.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Pavagada Solar Park is also known by which name?
questions.explanation: Pavagada Solar Park is also known as Shakti Sthala. Its development involved a land-lease model with local farmers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included in the list of important lakes and reservoirs of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Linganamakki is among the important reservoirs listed in the reference material for Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups consists entirely of reservoirs listed in the Karnataka geographical reference?
questions.explanation: Kabini, Harangi and Hemavathi are included in the reference list of important Karnataka lakes and reservoirs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an important reservoir associated with the Krishna River system in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Almatti is an important reservoir on the Krishna River. Ulsoor Lake, Sankey Tank and Hebbal Lake are also listed among Karnataka's important water bodies.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following water bodies is located in Bengaluru and appears in the reference list of important Karnataka lakes and tanks?
questions.explanation: Ulsoor Lake is one of the Bengaluru water bodies included in the reference list. Sankey Tank, Hebbal Lake and Bellandur Lake are also listed.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included in the list of important Karnataka lakes and reservoirs?
questions.explanation: Vanivilas Sagar is specifically included in the reference list of important Karnataka water bodies.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is identified in the reference as a protected landscape in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Sharavathi Valley is included among Karnataka's important wildlife and forest protected locations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which protected area is associated with the Biligiriranga Hills in southern Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Biligiri Rangaswamy Temple (BRT) protected landscape is associated with the Biligiriranga Hills and is important for wildlife conservation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is included among Karnataka's important wildlife sanctuaries and protected locations in the reference?
questions.explanation: Someshwara is listed among Karnataka's important wildlife and forest protected locations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only protected locations listed in the Karnataka reference material?

options.A: Brahmagiri, Pushpagiri and Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary

questions.explanation: Brahmagiri, Pushpagiri and Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary are all included in the reference list of Karnataka's important wildlife and forest protected locations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an atoll?

options.A: A ring-shaped coral reef or island enclosing a lagoon
options.B: A narrow passage connecting two seas

questions.explanation: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef or island enclosing a lagoon. It commonly develops around a subsiding volcanic island. Lakshadweep contains atolls.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which geographical feature is a long, narrow and deep sea inlet with steep sides, formed by glacial erosion?
questions.explanation: A fjord is a long, narrow, deep sea inlet with steep sides. It is formed by glacial erosion and later flooded by seawater. Fjords are common in Norway.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A depositional landform formed at a river mouth due to the accumulation of sediments is called:
questions.explanation: A delta develops when a river deposits sediments as it enters a standing water body. The river may divide into distributaries within the delta.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an estuary?

options.A: A coastal transition zone where river freshwater mixes with seawater
options.B: A fan-shaped deposit formed by wind
options.C: A raised riverbank formed by glacial activity

questions.explanation: An estuary is a coastal transition zone where freshwater from a river mixes with seawater. Estuaries are often affected by tides and are biologically productive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In common Indian geographical usage, the term watershed can refer to:

options.B: A drainage divide or a small hydrological planning unit

questions.explanation: In common Indian usage, watershed may mean a small hydrological planning unit or the divide separating drainage basins. In international usage, it can also mean the drainage area itself; context matters.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The area from which precipitation and runoff drain to a common outlet, such as a river, lake or reservoir, is known as:
questions.explanation: A catchment area is the geographical area from which precipitation and surface runoff flow towards a common outlet.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a drainage basin?

options.A: The land area drained by a river system and its tributaries
options.B: A shallow coastal water body separated by a sandbar
options.C: An area permanently covered by ice
options.D: A raised block of the Earth's crust

questions.explanation: A drainage basin is the land area drained by a river and its tributaries. It is bounded by drainage divides.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A fan-shaped sediment deposit formed where a stream emerges from a steep valley onto a flatter plain is called:
questions.explanation: An alluvial fan forms when a stream emerges from a steep valley onto flatter land and loses its ability to transport as much sediment. The sediments spread out in a fan-shaped deposit.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which landform consists of relatively flat land beside a river that is periodically inundated during floods?
questions.explanation: A floodplain is relatively flat land beside a river. It develops through sediment deposition and may be periodically flooded.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A natural raised riverbank formed by repeated flood deposition is known as:
questions.explanation: A levee may be a natural raised riverbank formed by repeated flood deposition or an artificial embankment constructed to confine floodwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An accumulation of unsorted rock debris transported or deposited by a glacier is called:
questions.explanation: A moraine consists of unsorted rock debris transported or deposited by glacial activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which glacial landform is described as a steep-sided, armchair-shaped hollow at the head of a glacial valley?
questions.explanation: A cirque is a steep-sided, armchair-shaped hollow at the head of a glacial valley. It may contain a small lake called a tarn.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A persistent mass of land ice formed from compacted snow and moving under gravity is called:
questions.explanation: A glacier is a persistent mass of land ice formed from compacted snow. It moves under the influence of gravity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an iceberg?

options.A: A large piece of freshwater ice that has broken from a glacier or ice shelf and floats in the sea
options.C: A submerged mountain chain in the ocean
options.D: A mass of glacial debris deposited on land

questions.explanation: An iceberg is a large piece of freshwater ice that breaks away from a glacier or ice shelf and floats in the sea. Most of its volume remains below the water surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A permeable geological formation that stores and transmits usable quantities of groundwater is called:
questions.explanation: An aquifer is a permeable geological formation capable of storing and transmitting usable quantities of groundwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An artesian well taps which type of aquifer?

options.A: An unconfined aquifer with no pressure
options.B: A confined aquifer in which water rises under pressure
options.C: An aquifer located only beneath glaciers
options.D: A saline aquifer connected directly to the ocean

questions.explanation: An artesian well taps a confined aquifer where groundwater is under pressure. Water rises in the well and may flow naturally at the surface if the pressure is sufficient.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A hot spring that periodically erupts jets of hot water and steam is called:
questions.explanation: A geyser is a hot spring that periodically erupts hot water and steam due to underground heating and pressure conditions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A natural discharge of groundwater heated by geothermal energy is known as:
questions.explanation: A hot spring is a natural discharge of groundwater that has been heated by geothermal energy.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A fertile area in a desert where water is available from a spring, well or groundwater discharge is called:
questions.explanation: An oasis is a fertile area in a desert where water is available, often through a spring, well or groundwater discharge.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A hill or ridge of sand deposited by wind is known as:
questions.explanation: A dune is a hill or ridge of wind-deposited sand. Its shape is influenced by wind direction, sediment supply and vegetation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Loess is primarily composed of which material?
questions.explanation: Loess is a blanket-like deposit of fine windblown silt. It is often fertile but can be susceptible to erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A landscape characterised by caves, sinkholes, disappearing streams and underground drainage is known as:
questions.explanation: Karst is a landscape developed through the dissolution of soluble rocks such as limestone. It commonly features caves, sinkholes, disappearing streams and underground drainage.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A long, steep slope or cliff separating two relatively level areas is called:
questions.explanation: An escarpment is a long, steep slope or cliff separating two relatively level areas. It may be associated with faulting or differential erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A long depression formed when a block of the Earth's crust subsides between approximately parallel normal faults is called:
questions.explanation: A rift valley is a long depression formed when a crustal block subsides between approximately parallel normal faults under extensional forces. The East African Rift is an example.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An uplifted or relatively elevated block of the Earth's crust bounded by faults is known as:
questions.explanation: A horst is an uplifted or relatively elevated block of the Earth's crust bounded by faults, commonly normal faults.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A down-dropped block of the Earth's crust bounded by faults is called:
questions.explanation: A graben is a down-dropped crustal block bounded by faults. It forms a structural valley and is the counterpart of a horst.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The gently sloping, submerged edge of a continent extending from the shoreline to the shelf break is called:
questions.explanation: The continental shelf is the gently sloping submerged margin of a continent, extending from the shoreline to the shelf break.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which ocean-floor feature represents the relatively steep descent from the continental shelf break towards the deep ocean basin?
questions.explanation: The continental slope is the relatively steep descent from the edge of the continental shelf towards the deep ocean basin.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A broad, very gently sloping region of the deep-ocean floor, commonly covered by fine sediments, is called:
questions.explanation: An abyssal plain is a broad, very gently sloping deep-ocean floor, commonly covered by fine sediments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A long, narrow and very deep depression on the ocean floor, usually associated with a subduction zone, is called:
questions.explanation: An ocean trench is a long, narrow and very deep depression in the ocean floor. Ocean trenches are usually associated with subduction zones.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Mid-ocean ridges are primarily formed at which type of plate boundary?
questions.explanation: A mid-ocean ridge is a submarine mountain chain formed mainly at divergent plate boundaries, where new oceanic crust is created.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A relatively dry region on the leeward side of a mountain range is known as:
questions.explanation: A rain-shadow region lies on the leeward side of a mountain range. Descending air is generally drier because much of its moisture has been lost on the windward side.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Rainfall caused when moist air is forced to rise over elevated terrain, cools and condenses is called:
questions.explanation: Orographic rainfall occurs when moist air is forced to rise over mountains or other elevated terrain. The rising air cools, condenses and produces rainfall.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a temperature inversion?

options.A: A condition in which temperature decreases rapidly with height
options.B: A condition in which temperature increases with height through a layer
options.D: A reversal in the direction of ocean currents

questions.explanation: Temperature inversion is an atmospheric condition in which temperature increases with height through a layer, opposite to the normal tropospheric lapse-rate pattern.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An isotherm is a line on a map joining places having equal:
questions.explanation: An isotherm joins places having equal temperature for a specified time or period.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which line on a weather map joins places having equal atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: An isobar joins places having equal atmospheric pressure at a specified time. Weather maps commonly use pressure values reduced to mean sea level.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A line joining places that receive equal rainfall over a specified period is called:
questions.explanation: An isohyet is a line joining places that receive equal amounts of rainfall over a specified period.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: An isobath represents points having equal:
questions.explanation: An isobath is a line joining points of equal water depth below a reference surface on a bathymetric map.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a delta from an estuary?

options.A: A delta is formed mainly by sediment deposition, whereas an estuary is characterised by tidal mixing of freshwater and seawater
options.B: A delta is formed by glacial erosion, whereas an estuary is formed by wind deposition
options.C: A delta is a deep ocean depression, whereas an estuary is a coral island
options.D: A delta is a mountain pass, whereas an estuary is a desert landform

questions.explanation: A delta is primarily a depositional landform formed by sediment accumulation and distributary channels. An estuary is a coastal transition zone characterised by tidal mixing of river freshwater and seawater. The Ganga–Brahmaputra is an example of a delta, while the Narmada and Tapi have estuarine mouths.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following sets of geographical features is correctly matched with its description?

options.A: Horst — down-dropped block; Graben — raised block; Moraine — windblown silt
options.B: Horst — raised fault block; Graben — down-dropped fault block; Moraine — glacial debris
options.C: Horst — river-mouth deposit; Graben — coral island; Moraine — coastal inlet
options.D: Horst — glacial hollow; Graben — sand ridge; Moraine — ocean trench

questions.explanation: A horst is a relatively raised block of crust bounded by faults, while a graben is a down-dropped block. A moraine is an accumulation of unsorted rock debris transported or deposited by a glacier.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river is conventionally given as the longest river in the world in the reference material?
questions.explanation: The Nile is the conventional answer for the world's longest river. However, the comparison with the Amazon is debated because river length measurements depend on the selected source and measurement method.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest desert in the world when cold deserts are also included?
questions.explanation: Antarctica is the largest desert overall because deserts are defined by low precipitation, not by high temperature.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which desert is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara is the largest hot desert. Antarctica is the largest desert overall, including cold deserts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the usual geographical convention that treats Australia as a continent, which is the world's largest island?
questions.explanation: Greenland is considered the world's largest island under the usual convention. Australia is classified as a continent rather than an island.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest inland water body in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: The Caspian Sea is the largest inland water body by surface area. Despite its name, it is an enclosed inland water body.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by surface area. Lake Baikal is the deepest lake and has the greatest freshwater lake volume.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which lake is the deepest in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake in the world. It also has the greatest freshwater volume among lakes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination correctly identifies the world geographical records of three major inland water bodies?

options.A: Caspian Sea — largest inland water body by area; Superior — largest freshwater lake by area; Baikal — deepest lake
options.B: Caspian Sea — deepest lake; Superior — largest inland water body; Baikal — largest hot lake
options.C: Caspian Sea — largest freshwater lake; Superior — deepest lake; Baikal — largest inland water body
options.D: Caspian Sea — smallest inland water body; Superior — deepest lake; Baikal — largest lake by area

questions.explanation: The reference distinguishes these records: the Caspian Sea is the largest inland water body by area, Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area, and Lake Baikal is the deepest lake and has the greatest freshwater volume.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Dead Sea region is associated with which geographical record?
questions.explanation: The Dead Sea region is associated with the lowest exposed land elevation. It should not be confused with the deepest point in the ocean.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the highest mountain summit above mean sea level?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest is the highest mountain summit above mean sea level. The jointly announced height in 2020 was 8,848.86 metres.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The deepest known ocean point, Challenger Deep, is located in which oceanic trench?
questions.explanation: Challenger Deep lies in the Mariana Trench and is identified in the reference as the deepest known ocean point.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river has the greatest average discharge in the world?
questions.explanation: The Amazon has the greatest average discharge of any river in the world and also has the largest drainage basin.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river has the largest drainage basin in the world?
questions.explanation: The Amazon River has the world's largest drainage basin. It also carries the greatest average volume of water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is recognised in the reference as the world's largest delta?
questions.explanation: The Ganga–Brahmaputra–Meghna Delta, also called the Bengal Delta, is the world's largest delta and is shared by India and Bangladesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the southernmost point of the entire Indian territory?
questions.explanation: Indira Point, located on Great Nicobar Island, is the southernmost point of India. Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which place is the southernmost point of mainland India?
questions.explanation: Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India. Indira Point is the southernmost point of the entire Indian territory.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which longitude is used as the Standard Meridian of India?
questions.explanation: India's Standard Meridian is 82°30′ East longitude. Indian Standard Time is based on this meridian.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Indian Standard Time (IST) is ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) by:
questions.explanation: Indian Standard Time is UTC+5:30. It is calculated using India's Standard Meridian at 82°30′ E.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How many Indian states are crossed by the Tropic of Cancer?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight Indian states. The reference highlights this as an important examination fact.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following states is NOT crossed by the Tropic of Cancer?
questions.explanation: Karnataka is not crossed by the Tropic of Cancer. It lies south of the Tropic of Cancer.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about the Tropic of Cancer and Karnataka is correct?

options.A: The Tropic of Cancer passes through northern Karnataka
options.B: The Tropic of Cancer passes through southern Karnataka
options.C: Karnataka is not among the eight states crossed by the Tropic of Cancer
options.D: The Tropic of Cancer forms Karnataka's southern boundary

questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly identifies Karnataka as a state that is not crossed by the Tropic of Cancer.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The River Ganga is formed at Devprayag by the confluence of which two rivers?
questions.explanation: The Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers meet at Devprayag in Uttarakhand. From this confluence, the river is known as the Ganga.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Devprayag is an important geographical location because it marks the confluence of:
questions.explanation: Devprayag is the confluence of the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers, where the river takes the name Ganga.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Godavari River originates near which place in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: The Godavari originates near Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Chilika Lake in Odisha is geographically classified as a:
questions.explanation: Chilika is a large brackish-water lagoon situated on the coast of Odisha.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is identified as India's largest inland salt lake?
questions.explanation: Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan is India's largest inland salt lake.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?

options.A: Chilika — Brackish-water lagoon; Sambhar — Inland salt lake
options.B: Chilika — Glacial lake; Sambhar — Freshwater tectonic lake
options.C: Chilika — Crater lake; Sambhar — Coastal lagoon
options.D: Chilika — Inland salt lake; Sambhar — Brackish-water lagoon

questions.explanation: Chilika is a brackish-water lagoon in Odisha, while Sambhar in Rajasthan is India's largest inland salt lake.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Nile and Amazon rivers according to the reference material?

options.A: The Nile has the greatest discharge, while the Amazon is conventionally the longest
options.B: The Nile is conventionally considered the longest, while the Amazon has the greatest discharge and largest drainage basin
options.C: Both rivers have the same discharge and drainage basin
options.D: The Amazon is conventionally the longest, while the Nile has the largest drainage basin

questions.explanation: The reference gives the Nile as the conventional longest-river answer, while identifying the Amazon as the river with the greatest discharge and largest drainage basin. The length comparison is debated.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the largest desert overall from the largest hot desert?

options.A: Sahara is the largest overall; Antarctica is the largest hot desert
options.B: Antarctica is the largest overall; Sahara is the largest hot desert
options.C: Gobi is the largest overall; Kalahari is the largest hot desert
options.D: Arabian Desert is the largest overall; Sahara is the second-largest hot desert

questions.explanation: Antarctica is the largest desert overall, while the Sahara is the largest hot desert. This distinction is an important examination point.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is Greenland identified as the world's largest island rather than Australia?

options.B: Australia is treated as a continent under the usual geographical convention
options.C: Australia is not surrounded by water
options.D: Greenland is located in the Southern Hemisphere

questions.explanation: Greenland is considered the largest island under the usual convention because Australia is classified as a continent rather than an island.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Dead Sea region from Challenger Deep?

options.A: Both represent the lowest exposed land elevations
options.B: The Dead Sea region is associated with the lowest exposed land elevation, while Challenger Deep is the deepest known ocean point
options.C: The Dead Sea is the deepest ocean point, while Challenger Deep is a land depression
options.D: Both are located in the Mariana Trench

questions.explanation: The Dead Sea region is associated with the lowest exposed land elevation. Challenger Deep, located in the Mariana Trench, is the deepest known ocean point.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about India's southernmost points is correct?

options.A: Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of the entire Indian territory
options.B: Indira Point is the southernmost point of mainland India
options.C: Indira Point is the southernmost point of the entire Indian territory, while Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India
options.D: Minicoy is the southernmost point of mainland India

questions.explanation: Indira Point is situated on Great Nicobar Island and is the southernmost point of India. Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which combination correctly represents India's Standard Meridian and the time difference of IST from UTC?
questions.explanation: India's Standard Meridian is 82°30′ E, and Indian Standard Time is UTC+5:30.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river is associated with Trimbakeshwar as its place of origin?
questions.explanation: The Godavari River originates near Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At which location does the Bhagirathi meet the Alaknanda to form the Ganga?
questions.explanation: The Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet at Devprayag, after which the river is known as the Ganga.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Lake Baikal is correct?

options.A: It is the largest inland water body by surface area
options.B: It is the largest freshwater lake by surface area
options.C: It is the deepest lake and has the greatest freshwater lake volume
options.D: It is the largest inland salt lake

questions.explanation: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake in the world and has the greatest freshwater volume among lakes. The Caspian Sea and Lake Superior hold different records.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Ganga–Brahmaputra–Meghna Delta is also commonly known by which name?
questions.explanation: The Ganga–Brahmaputra–Meghna Delta is also known as the Bengal Delta. It is shared by India and Bangladesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which state is associated with Chilika, the large brackish-water lagoon mentioned in the reference?
questions.explanation: Chilika is a large brackish-water lagoon located in Odisha.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Sambhar Lake, India's largest inland salt lake, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Sambhar Lake is located in Rajasthan and is identified in the reference as India's largest inland salt lake.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What height for Mount Everest is cited in the reference as the jointly announced 2020 measurement?
questions.explanation: The reference cites the jointly announced 2020 height of Mount Everest as 8,848.86 metres.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest continent in the world by area and population?
questions.explanation: Asia is the largest continent by both geographical area and population.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which continent is conventionally considered the smallest by area?
questions.explanation: Australia is conventionally considered the smallest continent by area. Oceania is a broader regional term that includes Australia, New Zealand and Pacific islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest and deepest ocean basin in the world?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean basin in the world.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the smallest and shallowest among the five commonly recognised oceans?
questions.explanation: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest of the five commonly recognised oceans.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is generally recognised as the longest river in Asia?
questions.explanation: The Yangtze, also called Chang Jiang, in China is generally recognised as Asia's longest river, with a length of approximately 6,300 km.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mountain is conventionally listed as the second-highest summit in the world after Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: K2, with an elevation of approximately 8,611 metres, is the world's second-highest mountain summit after Everest.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is listed as the third-highest mountain summit in the world?
questions.explanation: Kangchenjunga, at approximately 8,586 metres, is conventionally listed as the third-highest mountain summit in the world.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mountain is listed as the fourth-highest summit in the world?
questions.explanation: Lhotse, at approximately 8,516 metres, is listed as the fourth-highest mountain summit after Everest, K2 and Kangchenjunga.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which mountain is listed as the fifth-highest summit in the world in the reference material?
questions.explanation: Makalu, at approximately 8,485 metres, is listed among the world's highest peaks after Everest, K2, Kangchenjunga and Lhotse.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which country is generally ranked as having the longest coastline in the world?
questions.explanation: Canada is generally ranked as having the world's longest coastline. The exact measured length depends strongly on mapping scale and measurement method, a problem known as the coastline paradox.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the deepest lake in Africa?
questions.explanation: Lake Tanganyika is Africa's deepest lake and is also one of the deepest freshwater lakes in the world.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which lake, located on the Peru–Bolivia border, is commonly cited as the world's highest large navigable lake?
questions.explanation: Lake Titicaca lies on the Peru–Bolivia border in the Andes at approximately 3,812 metres above sea level. It is commonly cited as the world's highest large navigable lake.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest coral reef system, is located off the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef is situated off Queensland, Australia, and is the world's largest coral reef system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is generally identified as the world's largest peninsula?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Peninsula is generally identified as the world's largest peninsula.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the reference material, which peak is often identified as the highest peak entirely within Indian-administered territory?
questions.explanation: The reference identifies Nanda Devi, approximately 7,816 metres high, as the peak often given as the highest entirely within Indian-administered territory, subject to the precise territorial definition used. K2 is in territory claimed by India but administered by Pakistan.

options.B: Kangchenjunga is the highest peak on India's international border and is shared with Nepal

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the largest Indian state by geographical area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan is the largest Indian state by area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the smallest Indian state by geographical area?
questions.explanation: Goa is the smallest Indian state by area. Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep is the smallest and Ladakh is the largest by area.

questions.question: Which Union Territory is the largest in India by area?
questions.explanation: Ladakh is the largest Union Territory of India by area. Lakshadweep is the smallest Union Territory by area.

questions.question: Which Union Territory is the smallest in India by area?
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep is the smallest Union Territory in India by geographical area.

questions.question: Which river is commonly identified as India's longest river in standard examination material?
questions.explanation: The Ganga is commonly identified as India's longest river in standard examination material. Rankings can depend on whether the total transboundary course or only the Indian stretch is considered.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which river is the longest river of Peninsular India and is often called the Dakshin Ganga?
questions.explanation: The Godavari is the longest river of Peninsular India and is often called the Dakshin Ganga.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which lake is commonly described as one of India's largest freshwater lakes?
questions.explanation: Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir is commonly described as one of India's largest freshwater lakes. Its area fluctuates seasonally.

questions.question: Which Indian state has the longest coastline according to the revised official measurement cited in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states under the revised official measurement cited in the PDF.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which Indian state had the largest forest cover by area in the India State of Forest Report 2023 cited in the PDF?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh had the largest forest cover by area in the India State of Forest Report 2023. Forest cover by area and forest cover as a percentage of geographical area are different measures.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the approximate northern latitude limit of mainland India given in the reference?
questions.explanation: The approximate northern latitude limit of mainland India is 37°6′ N. The southern mainland extent is approximately 8°4′ N.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the approximate western longitude limit of mainland India?
questions.explanation: The approximate western longitude limit of mainland India is 68°7′ E. Its eastern longitude limit is approximately 97°25′ E.

questions.explanation: Including the islands, India's southern extent reaches approximately 6°45′ N at Indira Point on Great Nicobar Island.

questions.explanation: Kibithu, in Arunachal Pradesh, is commonly cited as India's easternmost location in examination references.

questions.explanation: Guhar Moti in Kutch, Gujarat, is commonly cited as India's westernmost location.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: The Indian Standard Meridian passes near which city in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Indian Standard Meridian at 82°30′ E passes near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Approximately how much does mean solar time change for every one degree of longitude?
questions.explanation: Every one degree of longitude corresponds to approximately four minutes of mean solar time. India adopts a single standard time based on 82°30′ E to maintain uniform civil time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: At which location do the Ganga and Yamuna meet?

questions.explanation: Rudraprayag is the confluence of the Alaknanda and Mandakini rivers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra enters Arunachal Pradesh from Tibet, where its upper course is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo. In Arunachal Pradesh it is called the Siang or Dihang. After joining major tributaries in Assam, it is known as the Brahmaputra.

questions.question: The Bhagirathi River, an important headstream of the Ganga, originates from which glacier region?
